A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original Stable Diffusion unlearning and fine-tuning experiments, scaling analyses, parameter ablations and one-dimensional simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated unlearning methods, incidental-resurgence measurements and fine-tuning sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The applied procedure remains concept unlearning followed by benign fine-tuning. The added algorithms are comparison methods; the new linear model supplies theoretical analysis rather than a revised applied unlearning method.

E1.justification: The four main erasure domains remain unchanged. v3 adds the distinct scenario of erased objects appearing under retained-object prompts, while removing v2's one-dimensional Gaussian/interval simulation.

E2.justification: v3 adds SalUn, Scissorhands (SHS) and EraseDiff to the four previously evaluated algorithms in the Stable Diffusion v1.4 comparisons and scaling analyses. The Stable Diffusion v2.1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Retained benchmark protocols remain unchanged. New designs include a paired incidental-resurgence evaluation over 2000 prompts and MACE sweeps over dataset size and fine-tuning steps. The simulation-specific likelihood and sampling protocol is removed; the newly stated default training recipe is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v3 adds scaling analyses for three additional algorithms, incidental-resurgence case studies and measurements, and MACE dataset-size and step-count sensitivity analyses. It removes the toy-model investigation. Existing ESD parameter ablations and UCE parameter comparisons remain despite relocation.

E5.justification: Both retain the stated three-seed benchmark evaluations and mean-plus/minus reporting. The UCE table's parenthesized intervals are unchanged. No revised run counts, uncertainty estimators or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark values and retained plots are unchanged, but substantial results are added. For example, v3 reports EraseDiff celebrity scores of 0.000 before fine-tuning and 0.693 afterward, plus incidental-resurgence and sensitivity results. v2's simulation results in Figures 5–6 are removed.

T1.justification: v2 provides a stylized simulation without theoretical guarantees. v3 introduces a linear diffusion formulation, subspace-erasure and overlap definitions, Proposition 5.1's gradient and curvature bounds, and supporting proofs in Appendices G–H.

C1.justification: The abstract's broad warning remains, but the introduction adds resurgence under unrelated generation prompts. It also replaces the exploratory toy-model contribution with a claimed provable characterization, including inevitability under nonzero subspace overlap in the linear setting.

C2.justification: The proposed explanation changes from smooth learned distributions and residual probability mass to gradient-subspace overlap and curvature amplification. The limitation of lacking theory becomes a limitation to linear theory, while incidental resurgence expands the interpretation of unintended user exposure.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies 1000 fine-tuning steps and LoRA, except where otherwise stated, including full-parameter fine-tuning for UCE. This documents retained experiments without establishing a setting change. Removing the toy experiment also removes its autograd and 2000-step numerical-integration instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion for SalUn, Scissorhands and EraseDiff, and removes the Aithal et al. mode-interpolation and Song et al. likelihood references associated with the toy investigation. The broader positioning around benign compositional-update vulnerabilities remains.

P1.justification: The title, authors, six main sections and much existing prose remain. Rewriting concentrates on the contribution summary, Section 5's explanatory narrative and the shortened discussion, with additional subsection and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 become v3 Table 1's two panels. The unchanged ESD ablation panels move from Figure 4 to Appendix Figures 16–17. Toy figures disappear, while new qualitative examples, scaling plots, incidental-resurgence displays and sensitivity plots substantially expand and rearrange the presentation.

improvement.justification: The added comparator coverage, incidental-resurgence tests, sensitivity analyses and training details strengthen the empirical paper. However, v3 replaces v2's cautious simulation-based explanation with a stronger theoretical contribution containing a substantive problem: Lemma H.1 asserts a bound for any update, while its proof selects a particular optimal step size. These empirical gains and the central theoretical rigor concern leave the net quality change uncertain.
